title: Intrinsic motivation of intensive care nurses. A professional biographical interview study. (MotivIn)
summary: The shortage of specialists in the field of intensive care has become even more acute following the coronavirus pandemic. Intensive care nurses are often confronted with changing shifts, a high workload and dealing with the critically ill and dying. Nevertheless, many intensive care nurses are highly motivated and committed to their work. We would like to investigate what exactly motivates intensive care nurses intrinsically in their profession. This is interesting in order to understand what makes this job so appealing to intensive care nurses. The results of our interview study may be of interest to employers. It is good for them to understand what drives their employees internally. In this way, the workplace can be adapted to these needs if necessary. This helps to ensure that intensive care nurses maintain their intrinsic motivation and stay in the job for a long time.
conditions: Motivation, intrinsische; Burnout, Cool-out, compassion fatigue

interventions.name: 10-20 nurses (with or without specialist training) working in intensive care at the time of the survey

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Nursing professional in nursing or paediatric nursing with completed state final examination
have been working in an intensive care unit for at least 1 year at the time of the survey
sufficient knowledge of German to conduct an interview
Exclusion criteria:
professional group other than nursing staff
No completed state final examination in nursing or paediatric nursing
Place of practice other than intensive care unit
worked in the intensive care unit for less than 1 year at the time of the survey
insufficient knowledge of German
